newsitem.title: USA: Lilly gains on expedited FDA drug review.
newsitem.headline: Lilly gains on expedited FDA drug review.

text.p: Eli Lilly and Co shares jumped Wednesday after the company said the U.S. Food and Drug Administration had granted priority review status to its new drug application for raloxifene, a drug candidate for prevention of postmenopausal osteoporosis.
Lilly was up two points to 115-5/8, off a high of 117-1/2.

The Indianapolis drugmaker, which reported second quarter results today, said the FDA had placed raloxifene on a six-month review schedule, in contrast to the standard 12-month review. The company intends to market the drug under the brand name Evista.
"The expedited review is the big thing helping the stock," said Smith Barney analyst Joshua Alpert.
"Also, the company had a very strong second quarter," he said, referring to Lilly's year-on-year 17 percent increase in worldwide sales to almost $2 billion.

Raloxifene is among the first in a new class of drugs called selective estrogen receptor modulators. Resarchers hope the drugs will provide an alternative to hormone replacement therapy in preventing postmenopausal health risks without mimicking estrogen's side effects in the breast and uterus.
Three special items reduced Lilly's second-quarter earnings by $3.90 a share, causing it to report a quarterly loss of $1.732 billion, or $3.14 a share.
Excluding the one-time events, net income for the quarter was $417.2 million, or $0.76 per share -- matching the First Call consensus estimate.
